investigations.name: draft-to-living-cell
investigations.title: From Draft to Living Cell
investigations.question:
How far can a cell be built compositionally — assembled from typed interfaces,
each specified as a *draft* before any mechanism is chosen, then compiled into
something that actually runs — and does that composition hold together into a
whole cell that lives and dies?
investigations.hypothesis:
Every recurring composition pattern in the cellular-interface paper can be
authored as an inert draft (typed, unit-bearing ports + a structural contract, with
no dynamics) and then *compiled* — by installing one conforming mechanism per
draft — into an executable that preserves the paper's interface exactly and
produces genuine dynamics. The same signature admits many mechanisms; the figures
compose; and the composition sustains a whole cell across growth, division, and
disintegration.
